variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: One-year-ahead change in return on net operating assets; Table 5 identifies ΔRNOA_{t+1} as the dependent variable. The paper does not state the exact subtraction formula/window for this dependent variable. RNOA at each date uses the operating-income and NOA component recipe given in the RNOA_t term of this model. Raw component fields: COMP.FUNDA: gvkey, datadate, fyear, sich, at, act, che, lct, dlc, dltt, dp, dvc, dvp, ni, msa, recta, xint, idit, pstk, tstkp, dvpa, ivao, mib, ceq, seq, sale, capx, mkvalt, oancf, ivncf, fincf, ppent, prcc_f, csho Preserve raw missing values and denominators; do not impute missing source components or force an observed classification.

Source formula: OI_t / Average NOA_t Source definition: Current RNOA = OI / Average NOA. OI = CNI + NFE. CNI is net income/loss (#172) minus preferred dividends (#19) plus the change in marketable-securities adjustment (#238) and the change in cumulative translation adjustment in retained earnings (#230). NFE = interest expense (#15) × (1−MTR) + preferred dividends (#19) − interest income (#62) × (1−MTR) + lagged #238 − current #238. MTR is the applicable highest federal rate plus 0.02: federal rates are 34% for 1989–1992 and 35% for 1993–2005. NOA = NFO + CSE + minority interest (#38), where NFO = FO − FA; FO = current debt (#34) + long-term debt (#9) + preferred stock (#130) − preferred treasury stock (#227) + preferred dividends in arrears (#242); FA = cash/short-term investments (#1) + long-term receivables, investments and advances to affiliated companies (#32); CSE = common equity (#60) + preferred treasury stock (#227) − preferred dividends in arrears (#242). The source preserves change notation for #238/#230 and does not give an arithmetic averaging interval for Average NOA. Raw component fields: COMP.FUNDA: gvkey, datadate, fyear, sich, at, act, che, lct, dlc, dltt, dp, dvc, dvp, ni, msa, recta, xint, idit, pstk, tstkp, dvpa, ivao, mib, ceq, seq, sale, capx, mkvalt, oancf, ivncf, fincf, ppent, prcc_f, csho Preserve raw missing values and denominators; do not impute missing source components or force an observed classification.

Source formula: I(LC_t = Shake-Out) Source definition: Indicator for the Shake-Out life-cycle category under the cash-flow-pattern proxy: default stage for the three patterns not assigned to the other theoretical stages: (−,−,−), (+,+,+), and (+,+,−), with signs ordered operating, investing, financing. Use Compustat GVKEY/year and effective-dated CCM links for CRSP age/market variables.
The future-profitability models do not report fixed effects.
The article does not specify clustered standard errors.
No weighting scheme is stated.
The paper reports a future-profitability regression but does not identify its estimator; keep the estimator choice as an implementation issue.
Construct the three lifecycle classifications, five-year A&R medians, annual ratios and source-based exclusions while retaining missing component values.

implementation_issues.description: The exact subtraction window for ΔRNOA_(t+1), ΔRNOA_t, ΔATO_t and ΔPM_t is not stated; the annual-difference reading is retained as the conservative source-consistent construction.
Average NOA appears in RNOA and ATO denominators, but the article does not specify the averaging interval; a one-year component window is retained for timing only, not treated as a resolved formula.
The source supplies federal rate plus 0.02 for 1989–2005; the t+1 dependent variable requires a 2006 RNOA, and the 2006 MTR is not specified.

Compustat item #32/#60 and preferred/marketable-security special-item mappings must be matched to current annual fields and preserve source-level missingness; current catalog labels do not prove vintage equivalence.

review_notes: Selected Model 1 is the principal direct comparison of life-cycle classifications. Model 2 adds a separate interaction test, rather than only additional controls.
Four non-reference stage indicators are estimated; the reference group is mature for CF/A&R or middle-aged for age quintiles. Reported stage levels include the intercept.
The cash-flow classification is deterministic. No construction regression is invented; the later stock-return application is excluded.
The three Table 5 Model 1 life-cycle proxies are retained with the shared firm-year outcome.
No local historical coverage confirmation was supplied; first-appearance history, special-item mappings and 2006 outcome coverage remain unverified.

No weighting scheme is stated.
The paper reports a future-profitability regression but does not identify its estimator; keep the estimator choice as an implementation issue.
Construct the three lifecycle classifications, five-year A&R medians, annual ratios and source-based exclusions while retaining missing component values.

implementation_issues.description: The exact subtraction window for ΔRNOA_(t+1), ΔRNOA_t, ΔATO_t and ΔPM_t is not stated; the annual-difference reading is retained as the conservative source-consistent construction.
Average NOA appears in RNOA and ATO denominators, but the article does not specify the averaging interval; a one-year component window is retained for timing only, not treated as a resolved formula.
The source supplies federal rate plus 0.02 for 1989–2005; the t+1 dependent variable requires a 2006 RNOA, and the 2006 MTR is not specified.

Compustat item #32/#60 and preferred/marketable-security special-item mappings must be matched to current annual fields and preserve source-level missingness; current catalog labels do not prove vintage equivalence.

review_notes: Selected Model 1 is the principal direct comparison of life-cycle classifications. Model 2 adds a separate interaction test, rather than only additional controls.
Four non-reference stage indicators are estimated; the reference group is mature for CF/A&R or middle-aged for age quintiles. Reported stage levels include the intercept.
The cash-flow classification is deterministic. No construction regression is invented; the later stock-return application is excluded.
